title: Every message that names a node says which node it is
name: Every message that names a node says
description:
This is where the complaint actually lands. A bare id is printed, joined by commas, in roughly fifteen places, and every one of them is a sentence a human reads with no other context:

- packages/mcp/src/render.ts:80 and :83 — the board's `waiting on …` tails
- packages/mcp/src/render.ts:46 — loose decisions
- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts:315 — what `bind` wrote
- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts:360 — `… it no longer holds a, b, c` after an answer
- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts:539 and :542 — briefs withdrawn, nodes flagged
- packages/mcp/src/tools/build.ts:29 — nodes heading for the same files
- packages/mcp/src/tools/distribute.ts:38, :114, :117 — assigned and passed over

Put the name beside the id in all of them, in one consistent form so a reader learns it once. Route it through whatever the data-flow decision settles rather than formatting it at each call site — fifteen hand-written formats is fifteen chances to print a different shape.

Two things the id is *not* decoration for and must survive verbatim: it is what the human types back into a tool, and it is the file name on disk. A message that prints only a name is a message nobody can act on. Update the tool tests in the same node — several assert on these exact strings.

brief.approach:
Score 5: one small function and about fifteen call sites, plus the tests that assert on the old strings. Mechanical, and the risk is doing it fifteen different ways.

**The field exists.** `Node.name` is required (`packages/schema/src/node.ts`, merged with `a-node-gets-a-short-name-a-person-can-re-xygw`) and every node on disk has one from the v7 backfill. Nothing to add there.

**One function, in the module that already shapes this surface's sentences.** The bound decision chose a formatter per surface; this node is the plugin's. Put it in `packages/mcp/src/render.ts`, unexported or exported as the file's other helpers are, taking the board and an id:

```ts
const named = (board: Board, id: string): string => {
	const name = board.nodes.get(id)?.name
	return name === undefined ? id : `${id} (${name})`
}
```

**The id survives verbatim, and that is not negotiable.** It is what the human types back into a tool and the file name on disk, so a message printing only a name is one nobody can act on. Id first, name in parentheses after it — one shape, learned once. Say that in the function's comment.

A node the board does not hold falls back to the bare id rather than throwing: these are message paths, and a broken record must not take a whole reply down (§8.4).

**For a list**, add a second helper that maps and joins, so `a, b, c` becomes one expression at every site rather than fifteen `.map(named).join(', ')` spellings that will drift.

**The call sites**, all in `packages/mcp/` — the node's own text lists them and the line numbers have moved since, so find them with `rg -n "join\(', '\)" packages/mcp/src`:

- `render.ts` — the board's two `waiting on …` tails, and the loose-decisions line. **Decisions are not nodes**: they have no `name` field, so leave every decision id bare. Getting this wrong is the likeliest mistake in the node.
- `tools/plan.ts` — what `bind` wrote; `… it no longer holds a, b, c` after an answer; briefs withdrawn and nodes flagged after an `edit_decision`.
- `tools/build.ts` — nodes heading for the same files.
- `tools/distribute.ts` — assigned and passed over.

Several of these do not have the board in hand at the point of printing — that is the cost the accepted decision names. Pass the board they already loaded a few lines above; do not load a second one inside a message helper, and do not reach for `loadBoard` inside `render.ts`.

**The tests assert on these exact strings and are part of this node.** `test/integration/mcp.test.ts` has cases matching `no longer holds`, the overlap warning and the distribute output. Update them to the new shape rather than loosening them to a substring match — a test that stops checking the sentence is a test that stops protecting it.

**Out of scope:** the terminal and the dashboard. The decision gives each surface its own formatter, and `the-terminal-and-the-dashboard-say-the-n-idmg` waits on this node and owns those two. Do not touch `packages/cli/src/out.ts` or anything under `apps/`.

acceptance.proves: every message that names a node now carries its name beside the id — the board tails, bind, the post-answer sentence, the overlap warning and distribute — asserted on the exact sentences rather than a loosened substring
decision ids stayed bare — a decision has no name field, and putting one there is the likeliest way to get this wrong
the call sites go through the one formatter rather than each interpolating its own shape — fifteen hand-written formats is fifteen chances to print a different one
the formatter takes the board it is given and never loads a second one inside a message path

acceptance.run: test -z "$(git diff --name-only development -- packages/cli apps packages/core packages/schema)"
acceptance.proves: the terminal and the dashboard were left alone — each surface gets its own formatter and that is a separate node
every changed call site has the board in hand at the point of printing
